Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Newport/Morehead City NC
753 PM EDT Wed Sep 9 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the previous forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Gradual warming through the rest of the week, peaking on
Thursday and Friday.

2) More unsettled pattern expected Friday through the weekend as
front stalls near the area.

3) Back to a more typical summertime pattern next week with high
draped over the southeast.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Latest surface analysis shows high pressure now
sitting off the coast of the mid-Atlantic while broad ridging
continues to expand over much of the CONUS' southern tier. Winds
across the area are now out of the south to southeast and
temperatures have climbed a few degrees from yesterday into the
mid to upper 80s. Dews have also jumped as well, into the low to
mid 60s.

Temperatures peak tomorrow and Friday as flow turns more
southwesterly and low-level thicknesses peak, with highs in the
low to mid 90s. Dew points also peak on Friday, resulting in
maximum heat index values returning to between 100-105. At this
time the odds of issuing a Heat Advisory look to be less than
10%, but trends will continue to be monitored.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Mid- level subsidence aloft will keep 
precipitation chances very subdued this afternoon despite the 
uptick in instability, although cannot completely rule out an 
isolated shower or two along typical sound and sea breeze 
convergence zones. Shortwave approaches from the central plains 
tomorrow, weakening the ridge and aiding in a slightly more 
favorable environment for isolated to widely scattered showers 
and thunderstorms.

Friday the high continues to shift offshore and a front sweeps 
south through the Mid-Atlantic region. Ahead of this front, 
continuous warm, moist advection in southerly flow will help 
build PWATs to near 2". This will bring scattered to numerous 
sea breeze showers/tstorms back in the forecast. After some
waffling the past few runs, guidance has come into far better
agreement showing the front largely bisecting eastern NC by
Friday, although a small minority still shows it stalling
farther north along the VA border. Wherever the boundary ends 
up setting up will be the focus for the highest risk of training
showers and thunderstorms contributing to a localized flash 
flooding threat. Forecast effective shear has trended down on 
Friday to generally less than 15 kt, so the risk of any stronger
storms is less than 5%.

The front lifts back north Saturday into Sunday as a shortwave
moves through the region. This shortwave will bring slightly
better chances for showers and thunderstorms this weekend. Like
Friday, flooding concerns remain the primary risk with PWATs
still around 2" but effective shear slightly higher at 15-20 
kt. Available instability remains a question mark for that day 
given potential convective evolution on Friday and the risk for 
lingering convective debris overnight and/or low stratus that 
may develop on the cooler side of the frontal boundary. The NBM 
probabilistic envelope has shifted slightly cooler for Saturday
but still remains high compared to both deterministic and MOS 
guidance, suggesting a cooler and therefore lower instability 
solution will prevail. If more instability can develop, the 
modest uptick in shear may provide a slightly more favorable 
environment for an isolated stronger storm or two.

There is higher confidence on a low- CAPE outcome Sunday. While
heavy showers and some thunderstorms are possible with the 
shortwave, the severe threat appears to be more muted.

KEY MESSAGE 3...A more typical summertime pattern will settle in
again early next week as a large high sits over the southeast.
Based on current model outputs, we have enough moisture and 
instability present for some afternoon/evening sea breeze 
convection early next week, but there are no larger scale
synoptic features of note that would promote any additional
forcing.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
VFR conditions will prevail at the terminals through the TAF
period. There is a low chance (10-20%) for shallow fog 
development late tonight, roughly 8-11z, where decoupling occurs 
but given low probabilities and limited impact continue to keep
out of the TAFs this cycle. 

Breezier day tomorrow as front approaches the north, and a few
gusts to 15-20 kt are likely both inland and across OBX
terminals especially after 18z. Could see an isolated
thunderstorm tomorrow, mainly along the sea breeze, although 
the risk of a strong storm is minimal.

NOTE: AMD NOT SKED has been appended to the EWN TAFs as the 
site is not transmitting through normal channels. The site is 
still reporting via telephone so it will be monitored, but not 
as frequently as when it is completely operational. The next 
closest ASOS is at Cherry Point (KNKT).

Outlook (Friday through Monday): A front is expected to 
approach the region and stall Friday and Saturday bringing a 
chance of showers and thunderstorms with periods of sub-VFR 
conditions possible. Shower and isolated thunderstorm threat
extends into Sunday before more typical summertime weather
returns Monday.

&&

.MARINE...
Benign marine conditions ongoing this afternoon with winds
generally out of the south to southeast at 5-10 kt and seas
around 2-3 feet. Quiet conditions expected through tonight, but
conditions deteriorate slightly tomorrow as southwest winds
increase ahead of an approaching front. SW winds will peak
around 15-20 kt late Thurs into Friday morning, and a few gusts
to 25 kt are possible across the Albemarle Sound and northern
waters. Probabilities of 25+ kt are around 20% and a potential
advisory was deferred for the midnight shift's consideration.

Outlook (Fri through Mon): A coastal trough may also set up 
Thursday night into Friday, bringing increased tstorm chances 
along the Gulf Stream. Front bisects area waters on Friday then
lifts northward on Saturday. Sub-SCA conditions expected but
shower and thunderstorm risk will continue at least into Sunday.

&&

.MHX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...None.
MARINE...None.
